title: Hierarchical decision timeline + sampled decision logs for smart routing observability
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement:

Smart routing (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants) produces multi-hop decision paths. Current telemetry only exposes coarse final routing choices and sparse traces, which makes it hard to: reproduce user-visible fallbacks, attribute latency/cost to routing hops, and debug why a request was routed to a lower-tier model or fallback variant.

This ticket adds a compact, sampled "hierarchical decision timeline" and enriched per-hop metrics to make routing decisions auditable and debuggable without overwhelming storage. Goals: deterministic sampling, low overhead at the edge, fixed-schema logs for indexing, and privacy-safe PII redaction.

Why different from previous work: Prior tickets focused on decision-level traces and per-hop logs. This work introduces (1) a canonical, lightweight timeline protobuf/json shape that can be reconstructed in the Console, (2) deterministic sampling keyed by tenant+request to preserve reproducible capture, and (3) per-hop aggregated counters embedded in the runtime for high-cardinality metric queries.

Key constraints & trade-offs:
- Storage vs fidelity: full capture of every hop for all requests would be prohibitively expensive. We will sample ~1% by default and provide config per-customer.
- Latency impact: synchronous exports are unacceptable for tail latency. Use async non-blocking enqueue to Kafka with bounded local queue + backpressure fallback that emits counter-only events.
- Cardinality: include a small set of indexed keys (decision_id, tenant_id, route_policy, model_variant, reason_code). Avoid logging raw prompts or token payloads; only log hash digests if needed for correlation.

Expected benefit:
- Faster incident debug and RCA (reproducible timeline).
- Better observability for cost/latency trade-offs of routing strategies.
- Ability to create Console views (per-route decision waterfall) and alert on unusual fallback rates.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical decision_timeline event emitted for sampled requests and stored in ClickHouse with schema (decision_id, request_id_hash, tenant_id, timestamp, hop_index, node_id, route_policy, model_variant, reason_code, queue_ms, compute_ms)
Deterministic sampling implementation (configurable rate) that uses fnv1a(tenant_id + request_id) mod 10000 < sample_threshold
Runtime exposes per-hop counters (fallback_count, successful_fastpath_count, avg_queue_ms) emitted to Metrics pipeline (Prometheus/ClickHouse) at 1m granularity
No request payload, prompt text, or raw tokens are stored in decision logs; any needed correlation keys are stored as 128-bit hex digests
Console provides a sample decision timeline view and a query to filter high-fallback tenants
Documented rollout and feature flagging; opt-out for customers who require zero decision logging
implementation_plan: 1) Define canonical event shape (proto + JSON shim) and add X-Redwood-Decision-Id header propagation. 2) Implement deterministic sampler in gateway edge (Go) + feature flag in config service. 3) Emit sampled decision_timeline events to Kafka topic redwood.decisions.timeline. 4) Consumer writes to ClickHouse with TTL and compression. 5) Add per-hop counters in runtime (C++/CUDA path) and expose to metrics exporter. 6) Console: render timeline and chart fallback rates; add saved query templates. 7) Add e2e tests and perf benchmark to ensure <0.5ms p95 added latency on gate.
technical_notes:
Event schema (example JSON line): {
  "decision_id": "dec-20250225-6b7d",
  "request_id_hash": "a1b2c3d4e5f6...",
  "tenant_id": "acct-42",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-25T15:34:12Z",
  "hops": [ {"hop_index":0, "node_id":"edge-eu-3", "route_policy":"region-prefer", "model_variant":"gptx-8q", "reason_code":"match", "queue_ms":3, "compute_ms":12 }, {"hop_index":1, "node_id":"pool-us-west-2", "route_policy":"tier-fallback", "model_variant":"gptx-4q", "reason_code":"capacity-limit", "queue_ms":8, "compute_ms":9 } ] }

Sampling: use FNV1a 64-bit on (tenant_id | request_id) to decide sample. Store sampling_rate per-tenant in config service.

Storage: ClickHouse table routing_decision_timeline (MergeTree) partitioned by toYYYYMM(timestamp), TTL 30d by default. Keep aggregate counters in Prometheus/ClickHouse metrics pipeline for long tail retention.

Privacy: redaction layer strips any user-provided IDs from headers unless allowlist enabled. Use K-anonymity review for sample sizes if customer requests.

Performance: enqueue only; if local queue > 2k events, drop to minimal counter emission with a counter increment (fallback_drop_count) to avoid latency amplification.
rollout_plan: Canary in staging: enable sampling=10% for internal tenants; monitor queue depth/producer lag
Gradual rollout to 5% of production traffic for non-P0 customers over 48h
Expose tenant-level config in Console and opt-out switch
Full rollout for P0 customers only after performance SLA validation and security review
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Design review completed with Infra and Console teams. Agreed on ClickHouse for storage and Kafka topic naming.
2025-02-15: Proto schema v1 checked into repo (proto/routing/decision_timeline.proto). Internal PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/312
2025-02-19: Edge sampler PoC implemented in gateway; measured 0.18ms median added latency. Queuing backpressure behavior validated under synthetic spike.
2025-02-22: Metrics team requested additional per-hop kernel_choice field to help correlate quantization regressions; added to schema v1.1
2025-02-25: ClickHouse table DDL and consumer skeleton merged. Preparing console mockups for PM review.
reviews: PM feedback (Rita Gomez): prefer tenant-level default sample 0.5% for non-enterprise to control costs; added to config defaults.
Security review (Jamal Brooks): confirm no prompt/token storage and implement header redaction; flagged for final audit.
Infra feedback (Yuki Sato): recommend bounded producer concurrency and circuit-breaker on Kafka writer; applied in runtime implementation.
